correctness.rationale: The source diagram and universal property were reconstructed directly. Truth-vector lattice closure yields 14 prime points and 37 algebra elements; the fixed-point extrema determine both modal operations. All 37 generator-induced maps preserve constants, both lattice operations and both modalities (104118 exact preservation assertions). Independent closure agrees with each image. Exact composition and image deduplication yield the stated rank polynomials, 31 idempotents, 33 generated images, 27 retract images and the six e^3=e^2 cases. Freeness proves these are all endomorphisms, so the finite computation is exhaustive for the exact object claimed.
residual_risks: No higher-generated free algebra or infinite extrapolation is claimed. No independent audit is claimed.

evidence: Theorem 5.1 constructs F and proves existence and uniqueness of each generator-induced homomorphism.
Section 6 lists eleven one-generated subdirectly irreducible homomorphic images, classified as quotient algebras.

Section 2 states that projective algebras are retracts of free algebras. Theorem 9.6 uses a retraction of a five-element free algebra in the smaller variety V(D4), not a census of retract subalgebras of F.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The source provides the construction and general retraction/projectivity relationship, but no rank distribution or selection of which of the 37 generator images give idempotents. Its eleven subdirectly irreducible quotients neither classify all subalgebra images nor give multiplicities. Theorem 9.6 concerns a different free algebra in a proper subvariety and does not dominate this F-specific exact classification.

value.rationale: The one-generated free positive S4 algebra is a natural finite object singled out by the primary paper, in contrast to infinite two-generated free algebras. Before computing, its retracts are motivated by the standard characterization of projective algebras as retracts of free algebras (source Section 2); the same paper uses a concrete retraction in Theorem 9.6. The complete proper-image and retraction census supplies exact data a researcher studying projectivity and one-variable substitutions can use. The known total 37 does not specify these data. This is a complete exact invariant of the natural object, not an arbitrary parameter slice; no additional general theorem is asserted or needed.
residual_risks: The contribution is a modest finite classification for one algebra, not a general classification of projective positive S4-algebras.
